text:
sophie: Heads up — AtlasPay reporting sustained 429s on their dedicated pool in eu-west. Customer reports ~8-12s queueing then 429s. Their config shows min_replicas=1, max_replicas=10 but only one instance ever comes up. Can we triage?

dave: On it. Any autoscaler events or provider errors in the logs?

sre-bot: AutoscalerEvent at 1854123410: scale_check requested=3 launched=0 error=\"rateLimitExceeded: provider API 429\"

jordan: Sounds like provider-side rate limiting during provisioning. Why didn't our warm pool kick in? Check warmup config and whether prewarmed instances exist for this customer.

maira: Config note: customer atlaspay has warmup_pool=false and min_replicas=1. Their spikePolicy is aggressive but provisioning calls are being rejected by provider.

dave: I'll run a repro and tail autoscaler + provisioner logs. Command I used: ```kubectl logs -f deployment/autoscaler -n redwood | grep atlaspay```

dave: Also hitting our internal simulate endpoint to push load: ```curl -s -X POST \"https://internal.api.redwood/simulate?customer=atlaspay\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" -d '{"qps":200}'```

sre-bot: ProvisionerError at 1854123442: VM creation failed: \"QuotaExceeded / rateLimitExceeded (429)\" last_attempts=5

sophie: CS already escalated. They flagged potential churn if this repeats. Need an immediate mitigation plan (manual prod steps + a longer-term fix).

jordan: Short-term: enable routing fallback to hosted for this customer (soft fallback within 2s) so user requests land on hosted model while we recover dedicated. I'll draft a routing policy. Need PG/finance signoff for cross-billing.

maira: Quick mitigation I can try: manual provisioning via cloud console sometimes bypasses burst API quota. I'll attempt to create 2 nodes in their pool from the console and attach.

dave: From repro: provider APIs enforce a per-minute token limit. We need exponential backoff + jitter and a retry budget in the autoscaler/provisioner. Also consider prefilling a tiny warm pool for customers with aggressive spikePolicy.

helix-support: Customer note: \"We saw ~12s latency then 429s. The errors persisted ~90s even after we reduced traffic. Please advise ETA and whether we'll get credits.\"

jordan: Opening provider support ticket now with request ID and traces. Plan: (1) maira tries console provisioning, (2) dave pushes a temporary fallback routing rule, (3) sophie coordinates CS message + credits proposal.

maira: Manual console provisioning succeeded — I created 2 nodes and attached to the pool. Traffic drained off queued requests and customer reports reduced 429s. :thumbsup:

sophie: Good recovery. We'll keep the fallback config until provider confirms quota window reset. Follow-ups: add alert on provider 429 spikes, add preflight probe to estimate time-to-provision, and implement a retry/backoff strategy in provisioner. Also re-evaluate warmup_pool defaults for high-spike customers.

jordan: I'll add a runbook entry for this scenario (provider rate limit -> manual console provisioning -> enable fallback routing -> contact provider).

sophie: Marking incident mitigated for now. Root cause: autoscaler/provisioner hit cloud provider rate limits during scale-up; lack of prewarmed capacity and no fast fallback routing caused customer-visible 429s.

(reacted with :eyes: by dave)
